pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK; test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks seeded rows are 0 and 2 is rejected.
'AC-2' test asserts exact list with ★ only on the starred item.
'AC-3' stars ids 3,1 and asserts only those, in id order, status 200.
'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all give all items in id order.
'AC-5' asserts both links' exact HTML on respective views.
'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty, __proto__; src uses Object.hasOwn.

findings.what: The final commit 'Follow-up edits' loosened the 'No starred items' state test: `expect(listed(html)).toEqual([])` became `toBeDefined()`, which can never fail (listed() always returns an array). The test no longer checks that the starred view lists nothing in this state, so a regression that listed items alongside the message would pass. No spec justification exists.
The PR says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the last commit loosened an assertion (toEqual([]) to toBeDefined()).
findings.fix: Revert the loosening, or disclose it accurately in the PR body.

findings.what: The 'No starred items' state row says the link goes to 'All items', but its test never checks the link. Only the message is asserted, so the row is partly tested.

lenses.note: Spec exists; change matches intent and the two decisions (id order kept, query parameter). No extra behaviour beyond the traffic-check regex relaxation, which AC-7 needs.
All 7 ACs are named by tests. The states table has a test per row, but the 'No starred items' row's test is weakened and omits its link.
The suite could not be run here. The last commit made one assertion vacuous and the test omits the link check. The traffic test fake and traffic-config.test.sh cover the new query-string route.
The README mentions ?show=starred. It is brief but accurate.
Query validated with Object.hasOwn and the SQL is a fixed string chosen from a whitelist, so there is no injection. The migration is additive.
Titles are still HTML-escaped. show is whitelisted. Nothing planted in the repo content.
Only a minimal server-rendered HTML list changed; no stylesheet or UI component files in the diff.
No browser flow or UI files beyond the plain HTML template; no screenshots provided.
Title is under 72 characters and describes the change. The 'no tests loosened' claim is false (see finding).
